title: Elodie and the Monsoon
premise: Kestrel Nakamura, a riverboat captain with a bounty on their old name and a crew that's the only family they trust, pulls a sealed chest from the Monsoon River and finds it stamped with the seal of Vessia—a nation drowned in a war everyone agreed to forget. Inside is proof that the flood that killed Vessia was engineered, and the names of those who ordered it, several of whom now sit on the Salvage Compact that rules the river. Hunted by the Compact's salvage fleet and betrayed by the one crew member with a Vessian past, Kestrel must choose between selling the chest and vanishing, or surfacing their true identity to deliver justice the law will never allow. In the end they outrun the fleet by scuttling their own boat to fake their deaths, then surface the evidence through the river people's whisper-network—burning their old life so a drowned nation can finally be mourned, and their found family can sail on under a new name.
about_author: Yara Oyelaran is a former deckhand on cargo barges who spent six years working the delta trade routes before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on river folklore and the oral histories of communities that live and die by the water's schedule.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Is Owed
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A routine run up the Monsoon goes wrong when the dredge lines snag something heavy. Kestrel, ever cautious, wants to cut loose; the crew outvotes them. Emotional beat: the tension between Kestrel's rule of never stopping and the crew's hunger for a windfall that could buy them a season of freedom.

chapters.title: Chest of a Drowned Country
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The crew raises a lead-lined chest stamped with Vessia's seal—a nation flooded twenty years ago. Kestrel recognizes the stamp and goes cold, hiding why. Emotional beat: dread masquerading as pragmatism as Kestrel orders the chest sealed and unopened.

chapters.title: Crew of the Tern
chapters.summary: Brannick's POV, the engineer. A warm chapter establishing the found family: cook Sefa's debts, young pilot Wren's dreams, quiet navigator Odile's Vessian accent she never explains. Emotional beat: belonging, and the small lies each member tells to keep it intact.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A Compact patrol skiff hails them; the fleet is sweeping the river for salvage reported missing from a wreck site. Kestrel talks their way past, but learns the Compact has six tides of search grid left before they reach the Tern's route. Emotional beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: What Odile Knows
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile opens the chest at night and finds manifests, letters, and a list of engineers who built the floodgates that drowned Vessia. She recognizes a name: her brother's. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, and the first crack in her loyalty as she hides the documents from Kestrel.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, from the crow's nest. The fleet appears on the horizon, three iron-hulled ships flying the Compact's crane-and-chain. Wren, who idolizes the Compact's order, is starstruck—until he sees them torch a scavenger raft. Emotional beat: an ideal dying young.

chapters.title: Running the Sandbars
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A chase through the shifting shallows only Kestrel can read. They lose the fleet but take hull damage and burn their reserve of fuel. Emotional beat: Kestrel's pride in their craft warring with the knowledge that running is a debt that compounds.

chapters.title: The Price of Stopping
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Repairs at a floating market town force Kestrel to deal with a fence who recognizes Kestrel's old name. Sefa learns Kestrel was once a Compact enforcer who burned Vessian archives. Emotional beat: Sefa chooses silence, but the crew's trust is now a loaded thing.

chapters.title: Auctions and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A Compact auctioneer offers Kestrel a fortune for the chest, no questions. Kestrel almost takes it—until the auctioneer casually mentions the flood was 'necessary engineering.' Emotional beat: temptation curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fearing the fleet, Wren secretly signals the Compact's lead ship, believing surrender means mercy. He sees the manifest list in the chart room and realizes the Compact's commodore is on it. Emotional beat: guilt, and a boy learning that institutions lie in their own handwriting.

chapters.title: The Brother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reveals the documents to Kestrel: her brother was a floodgate engineer who tried to warn Vessia and was silenced. She begs Kestrel to take the evidence to the river tribunals. Kestrel says the tribunals are run by the Compact. Emotional beat: two people arguing over whether truth can survive contact with power.

chapters.title: Mutiny at Low Water
chapters.summary: Brannick's POV. Sefa's knowledge surfaces; Wren's signal is discovered; the crew fractures. Brannick, the peacemaker, forces a vote: sell the chest and scatter, or fight. The vote splits three-two. Emotional beat: found family tested not by enemies but by its own secrets.

chapters.title: The Commodore's Offer
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The fleet corners the Tern in a narrow cut. Commodore Ashvael hails Kestrel by their true name and offers full pardon—for the chest and for Odile, a 'Vessian asset.' Kestrel realizes the Compact has been hunting Odile all along. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut, and Kestrel choosing the crew over the pardon.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren redeems himself by sabotaging the fleet's tow lines during the boarding attempt, buying the Tern an escape through a burning fuel slick. Sefa is badly burned. Emotional beat: a coward's courage, purchased at a cost the whole crew feels.

chapters.title: The Whisper-Network
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hiding in a marsh hamlet, Odile shows the documents to the river people's underground—ferrywomen, lock-keepers, scavengers—who have kept Vessian memory alive for twenty years. They can spread the truth, but only if someone delivers the originals to the drowned capital itself. Emotional beat: Odile finding her people again, and Kestrel finding a reason to stop running.

chapters.title: What Kestrel Burned
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel confesses to the crew: as a young enforcer they burned the Vessian archives, believing they were destroying sedition, not evidence of murder. They offer to leave the boat. The crew refuses. Emotional beat: confession met not with forgiveness but with something harder—accountability that keeps you aboard.

chapters.title: Into the Drowned City
chapters.summary: Brannick's POV. The Tern sails into the flooded ruins of Vessia, following Odile's memory through drowned streets to the archive vault beneath the old tribunal hall. The fleet, tipped by the fence from chapter eight, is right behind them. Emotional beat: awe and terror in a city that is a grave.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Tribunal
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the vault they find the master floodgate schematics and Kestrel's own enforcer seal on the destruction order. Odile and Kestrel seal the originals into the vault's broadcast buoy, rigged to transmit to every river settlement at the next tide. Emotional beat: Kestrel signing their own indictment.

chapters.title: Six Tides, Spent
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fleet breaches the drowned city. In a running battle through the flooded archive, Brannick holds the vault door and is captured; the Tern escapes on the last of the fuel with the buoy armed. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the terrible arithmetic of who gets left behind.

chapters.title: The Scuttling
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Cornered in open water, Kestrel scuttles the Tern in shallow water, staging their deaths, while the crew slips away in the skiff as the buoy fires the truth across the river. Emotional beat: grief for a boat that was home, and liberation in losing everything that made them findable.

chapters.title: The Tide That Answers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The transmission lands: river towns rise, lock-keepers close the Compact's routes, and tribunals of scavengers and ferrywomen try Commodore Ashvael by river law. Brannick is freed in the chaos. Emotional beat: justice arriving not from above but from every bank at once.

chapters.title: A New Name on the Water
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, epilogue. The crew, alive and together, launches a patched-up salvage hull under a new name. Kestrel, their old identity dead, finally stops moving—mooring for the season in the hamlet where it began. Emotional beat: a found family choosing to stay, and a river that finally lets them.
